editorialStatus: Source-transcribed pathways; suggested documentation is not an insurer-provided checklist

guides.heading: Step therapy and clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The statewide drug list says step through metformin. The detailed guideline supplies indication-specific routes, including heart failure and CKD routes without a metformin trial requirement.

pathways.title: Type 2 diabetes
all: Patient is at least 10 years old.
Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
History of metformin failure at a minimum 1,500 mg daily for 90 days, OR contraindication, OR intolerance to metformin.

pathways.title: Adult type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease
all: Medication is requested to reduce cardiovascular death risk in an adult with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
History of metformin failure at a minimum 1,500 mg daily for 90 days, OR contraindication, OR intolerance to metformin.

pathways.title: Adult heart failure OR adult CKD at risk of progression
all: Medication is requested to reduce cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in an adult with heart failure; OR to reduce eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization in an adult with CKD at risk of progression.
No metformin trial is specified for this qualifying guideline pathway.

documentationSuggestions: Record the indication and supporting diagnosis.
For a metformin-dependent pathway, document the dose, dates, duration and response; alternatively document the specific contraindication or intolerance.
For the heart failure or CKD pathway, document the qualifying condition and clinical rationale.
guides.guidelineCaution: The statewide drug list flags step therapy rather than an explicit general PA requirement. The separate statewide clinical guideline is titled Prior Authorization; the plan determines the actual claim and authorization workflow.

guides.heading: Prior authorization clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The guideline permits either the specified prior-insulin pathway OR a clinical reason the patient needs concentrated insulin.

pathways.title: Prior insulin failure, intolerance or contraindication
all: History of failure, intolerance, or contraindication to insulin aspart OR insulin lispro.
History of failure, intolerance, or contraindication to Lantus.

pathways.title: Clinical need for concentrated insulin
all: There is a reason or special circumstance that the patient needs a concentrated insulin product.

documentationSuggestions: For the prior-insulin pathway, record which rapid-acting insulin and Lantus were tried, treatment outcomes, or the reason each cannot be used.
For the concentrated-insulin pathway, document the patient-specific reason a concentrated insulin formulation is needed.
guides.guidelineCaution: The guideline does not specify a universal insulin-dose threshold or an additional required laboratory test. Do not infer one.

guides.heading: Mounjaro prior authorization clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The November 2026 AHCCCS GLP-1 guideline specifies the following requirements for Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes. All criteria apply.

pathways.title: Type 2 diabetes — all requirements
all: Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus documented in submitted medical records.
Baseline hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%; the laboratory report MUST be submitted.
Either: paid claims verifying metformin failure at ≥1,500 mg/day for 90 days; OR documented metformin contraindication or intolerance.
Patient is at least 10 years old.
Medication is not being used for weight loss.
Provider attests no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor-containing drug, OR provides a plan to address concomitant use.
Medication is not being co-administered with another GLP-1 receptor agonist.

documentationSuggestions: Submit a baseline A1c laboratory report showing ≥6.5%, plus chart records confirming type 2 diabetes.

For metformin treatment failure, verify ≥1,500 mg/day for 90 days through paid pharmacy claims (the guideline explicitly requires paid-claim verification); otherwise document contraindication or intolerance.
Document the intended indication and review concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor and GLP-1 receptor agonist use.
guides.guidelineCaution: This guideline is for type 2 diabetes; the source states weight-loss/appetite-suppression requests are plan exclusions. Its 'Preferred Drugs' section names Mounjaro, but that heading does not override the separate current statewide drug-list preference field or establish a particular plan's benefit.

guides.heading: Trulicity prior authorization clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The November 2026 AHCCCS GLP-1 guideline names Trulicity in the same preferred-products qualification branch as Mounjaro. All the listed type 2 diabetes requirements apply.

pathways.title: Type 2 diabetes — all requirements
all: Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus documented in submitted medical records.
Baseline hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%; the laboratory report MUST be submitted.
Either: paid claims verifying metformin failure at ≥1,500 mg/day for 90 days; OR documented metformin contraindication or intolerance.
Patient is at least 10 years old.
Medication is not being used for weight loss.
Provider attests no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor-containing drug, OR provides a plan to address concomitant use.
Medication is not being co-administered with another GLP-1 receptor agonist.

documentationSuggestions: Submit a baseline A1c laboratory report showing ≥6.5%, plus chart records confirming type 2 diabetes.

For metformin treatment failure, verify ≥1,500 mg/day for 90 days through paid pharmacy claims (the guideline explicitly requires paid-claim verification); otherwise document contraindication or intolerance.
Document the intended indication and review concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor and GLP-1 receptor agonist use.
guides.guidelineCaution: The guideline's preferred-products branch applies to Trulicity for type 2 diabetes, not to other products merely because they contain a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Weight-loss/appetite-suppression requests are excluded under this guideline. The guideline's preference heading is not a replacement for the drug-list classification.
